definition: Deface means to ruin or injure the appearance of something.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word deface. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know deface should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Election posters seldom survive a weekend downtown before somebody defaces them with devil horns and blacked-out teeth.
A smudge is far milder than defacement — the smallest insult a surface can take, gone with one wipe; to deface something leaves a mark that will not wipe away.
Destroy goes further than deface — a defaced mural still hangs there, hurt but present; a destroyed one is simply gone.

Disfigure is the deeper injury — a face or form marred for good, so the shape itself reads differently ever after. Deface can be one ugly mark on a surface; the thing underneath is still whole and still itself.

The foundry poured the mayor's statue in 1911, and for ninety years the only marks on it were rain streaks.
Then came the decade of paint pens, and taggers began defacing it.
The parks department now waxes the bronze twice a year, because ink lifts off wax but bites into raw metal, and every tag ground away takes a sliver of the sculptor's chisel work with it.

Deface is the exact word for what the taggers do, because it means to ruin or injure the appearance of something — the statue still stands, still holds its shape; what suffers is its face, the surface the city actually sees.
Destroying it would take it away entirely; defacing it leaves the thing whole and makes you wince at it.
